newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech A-Invest says put under FinMin control.
newsitem.headline: Czech A-Invest says put under FinMin control.

text.p: A-Invest, the investment arm of the fifth largest Czech bank Agrobanka a.s., said on Wednesday that it had been put under the forced administration of the Czech Finance Ministry.
But Pavel Dvoracek, director of A-Invest, told Reuters that the ministry had yet to give a reason why the action was taken.
"The reason wasn't given, but we were unofficially told that control of A-Invest was underway," Dvoracek told Reuters.

A-Invest had been one of the most active participants in the Czech equities market, and was managing three mutual funds, including the large AGB OPF fund which reported assets totalling 2.4 billion crowns at the end of 1996.
Earlier, the Czech news agency CTK quoted an unnamed ministry regulator as saying that Jan Motycka was appointed to manage A-invest for the Finance Ministry.
Further details were not yet available, and Finance Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.
In December the ministry put the investment fund AGB IF 2, a major shareholder of Agrobanka a.s., under forced administration, but few details of the action have been disclosed.
CTK reported on Wednesday that, it had information showing that Agrobanka had sold A-invest to the secretive investment group known as Motoinvest.
The report of the sale to Motoinvest could not be independently confirmed.
Dvoracek said that as far as he knew, the forced administration of A-invest had nothing to do with the ministry's seizure of control of AGB IF 2.
In the summer, the Czech National Bank put Agrobanka itself under what the central bank called "temporary forced administration" with liquidity problems.
Agrobanka is still under control of the central bank, which is currently organising a tender in search of a strategic partner to take a controlling interest in Agrobanka.
